scenarioStory.history: Patient reports gradually worsening shortness of breath and productive cough with thicker, darker sputum over the past 2 days. Denies fever or chest pain. Has used his rescue inhaler more than usual with only partial relief. No recent travel, no known sick contacts. Lives alone, was able to walk to the door for EMS but stopped twice to catch his breath.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 67-year-old male with known COPD seated upright in a recliner, mildly tachypneic with audible expiratory wheezing and pursed-lip breathing. He is alert and able to speak in full sentences with occasional pauses. → Oxygen and DuoNeb administered: Crew applies nasal cannula oxygen and begins a nebulized albuterol/ipratropium (DuoNeb) treatment. Patient tolerates the treatment well without signs of severe distress requiring NIV escalation. → Symptoms improve without CPAP: Patient's respiratory distress continues to improve with oxygen and nebulized bronchodilator therapy. Work of breathing decreases, wheezing diminishes, and SPO2 normalizes. Prepared for transport without need for CPAP.

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 67-year-old male with known COPD seated upright in a recliner, mildly tachypneic with audible expiratory wheezing and pursed-lip breathing. He is alert and able to speak in full sentences with occasional pauses.
relatedChecklist: Obtain history of onset, triggers, prior treatments, and full vital signs including SPO2
Apply nasal cannula oxygen titrated to 94-98% SPO2 (permissive hypoxia to 90% acceptable given COPD)
Albuterol 5 mg nebulized with Ipratropium 0.5 mg nebulized (DuoNeb) for bronchospasm

scenarioEvents.name: Oxygen and DuoNeb administered
scenarioEvents.description: Crew applies nasal cannula oxygen and begins a nebulized albuterol/ipratropium (DuoNeb) treatment. Patient tolerates the treatment well without signs of severe distress requiring NIV escalation.
relatedChecklist: Reassess vital signs, SPO2, and work of breathing; document response to treatment

scenarioEvents.name: Symptoms improve without CPAP
scenarioEvents.description: Patient's respiratory distress continues to improve with oxygen and nebulized bronchodilator therapy. Work of breathing decreases, wheezing diminishes, and SPO2 normalizes. Prepared for transport without need for CPAP.

scenarioEvents.name: Bronchodilator therapy delayed
scenarioEvents.description: Nebulized bronchodilator therapy is delayed despite clear bronchospasm findings. The patient's work of breathing and hypoxia progressively worsen, now showing early signs of a more severe exacerbation.
relatedChecklist: Initiate DuoNeb without further delay: Albuterol 5 mg + Ipratropium 0.5 mg nebulized
